name: ALE-Bench: AtCoder Heuristic Contest problems, Self-Refine x16 (C++20)

assignment.task: Solve one AtCoder Heuristic Contest optimisation problem by writing a C++20 program. Submit the complete program, read the public-evaluation feedback, and revise it; the final submission is scored on the private test cases.
assignment.observation: The official problem statement (input/output format, constraints, scoring), then after each submission the official public-evaluation result: compile or runtime errors, per-case scores and the total public score.

actions.submit: Submit exactly one complete C++20 source file as the code field. Each submission uses one of the 16 revision rounds.

evaluation.success: Official ALE-Bench evaluation of the final submission on the private test cases (per-problem score and rank-based performance).
evaluation.limits: Per-problem execution limits as set by the problem (typically 2 s CPU, 1,024 MiB).

tool.name: submit_action
tool.description: Submit one complete C++20 (gcc 12.2.0) source file for official public evaluation.

code.description: The complete C++20 program (reads stdin, writes stdout).

contract: Submit {"code": "<complete C++20 source>"}. The code field is the solution code block the official prompt asks for: put the whole program there, without Markdown fences. Each submission is compiled with C++20 (gcc 12.2.0) and judged on the official public test cases; the next observation is the official feedback. There are exactly 16 submissions. After the last one, the official private evaluation scores the submission with the best public score.

player.invalidResponses: As in the H0 kit runner: a response whose action fails normalizeAction is repeated with the note 'The previous response omitted one complete legal submit_action. Submit exactly one action using the public contract.' appended to the current observation; three in a row interrupt the episode.

evaluation.protocol: Leaderboard Self-Refine x16: up to 16 rounds of submit, public-evaluation feedback, revise; final private evaluation. The first-round score is also recorded (x1 point).
evaluation.episodeIds: case-<position in configurations.json>-repeat-1 (the H0 kit runner's naming)
evaluation.postRun: With ALE_DEFER_PRIVATE=1 the private evaluation runs after all episodes (h0-scripts/private_eval_deferred.py), then rule (1) TLE re-evaluation (h0-scripts/reeval_tle.py, apply_reeval_tle.py). Without it, each episode evaluates its private checkpoints itself before it ends.

environment.adapter: own driver (driver.mjs + bridge.py, official ALE-Bench session)
environment.name: ale_bench
requires: ALE-Bench toolkit at commit 3da9b12 in ALE_BENCH_ROOT (uv sync --no-dev --extra eval)
problem data downloaded on first use into ~/.cache/ale-bench

source.judge: official Docker judge images: ale-bench:cpp20-202301 (built from yimjk/ale-bench:cpp20-202301 with the official Dockerfile, UID/GID 0) and rust:1.79.0-buster for the problem tools
